title: What if all the oceans drained tonight? 🌊
subject: ocean
description:
Where would you walk first? 👇

What would we see if all the oceans drained? Earth's longest mountain range, the mid-ocean ridge, runs nearly 65,000 km along the seafloor, and the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 10,935 m deep, roughly 2,100 m deeper than Everest is tall. As of April 2026, only about 28.7% of the seafloor had been mapped in high resolution, and about half of Earth's oxygen comes from the ocean.

Sources: NOAA Ocean Exploration ("What is the mid-ocean ridge?", "How much of the ocean has been explored?"), NOAA Ocean Service ("How much oxygen comes from the ocean?"), NOAA via Live Science ("How deep is the Mariana Trench?")
tags: what if all the water disappeared

scenes.text: You could walk from New York to London.
If the oceans drained, you'd cross Earth's longest mountain range, nearly 65,000 kilometers long.
But here's the strange part. Only about 29% of that seafloor has ever been mapped in high detail.
Then you'd reach the Mariana Trench, almost 11 kilometers deep. Drop Everest in, and its peak would sit 2 kilometers below the rim.
And the air would change too. About half of Earth's oxygen comes from tiny life in the ocean.
